subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn
question_text: Which of the following countries shares the longest international boundary with Ethiopia?

option_c: Kenya
option_d: Sudan
explanation: Somalia shares the longest boundary with Ethiopia.

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn
question_text: The shape of Ethiopia is best described as:

option_c: Compact
option_d: Elongated
explanation: Ethiopia has a relatively compact shape with a low boundary-to-area ratio.

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn
question_text: Which of the following is an advantage of a compact shape country?

option_c: Difficult to manage
option_d: Easy for defense and socio-economic integration
explanation: Compact shapes facilitate easy administration, defense, and integration.

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn
question_text: The total area of Ethiopia is approximately:

explanation: Ethiopia covers an area of approximately 1,106,000 square kilometers.

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn
question_text: In which geologic era did the formation of basement rocks (Precambrian) occur?
option_b: Precambrian Era
option_c: Cenozoic Era
option_d: Paleozoic Era
explanation: Basement complex rocks were formed during the Precambrian era.

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn
question_text: Which geologic era is known as the era of marine transgression and regression in Ethiopia?
option_b: Paleozoic Era
option_c: Mesozoic Era
option_d: Precambrian Era
explanation: Mesozoic era is characterized by sedimentary rock formation due to sea advances and retreats.

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn
question_text: During which geologic period was the Main Ethiopian Rift Valley formed?
option_b: Quaternary period
option_c: Jurassic period
option_d: Tertiary period of Cenozoic Era
explanation: The Rift Valley formed mainly during the Tertiary period of the Cenozoic era due to tectonic faulting.

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn
question_text: Which of the following sedimentary rocks was formed during the Mesozoic era in Ethiopia?
option_a: Adigrat sandstone, Hintalo limestone, and Upper sandstone
option_b: Basement complex
option_c: Alluvial deposits
option_d: Trap series basalt
explanation: Adigrat sandstone, Hintalo limestone, and Upper sandstone are classic Mesozoic sedimentary formations in Ethiopia.

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn
question_text: Rock formation in Ethiopia is notably absent during which era?
option_b: Paleozoic Era
option_c: Precambrian Era
option_d: Cenozoic Era
explanation: Due to prolonged erosion, rock formation is largely absent during the Paleozoic era in Ethiopia.

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn
question_text: Which physiographic region of Ethiopia covers the largest percentage of the country's total land area?
option_b: The Afar Depression
option_c: The Northwestern and Southeastern Highlands
option_d: The Western Lowlands
explanation: The highlands (above 1,000m) cover over 65% of Ethiopia's total area.

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn

option_b: Gambella plains
option_c: Lake Tana

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn

option_c: Northern and Southern massifs
option_d: nan
explanation: The Rift Valley splits the massive plateau into Northwestern and Southeastern highlands.

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn
question_text: Which of the following is the highest peak in Ethiopia?
option_b: Mount Ras Dashen
option_c: Mount Guna
option_d: Mount Batu
explanation: Mount Ras Dashen in the Simien Mountains is the highest peak (4,550m).

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn

option_d: nan

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn

explanation: The Nile river basin flows northward into the Mediterranean Sea.

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn

option_b: Baro-Akobo Basin
option_c: Awash Basin
option_d: Wabi-Shebelle Basin
explanation: Abay basin covers the largest area and carries the largest volume of water.

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn

option_b: It is an inland drainage system that ends in Lake Abbe

option_d: It drains into the Atlantic Ocean
explanation: Awash is an inland river basin terminating in lakes and salt pans in the Afar depression (Lake Abbe).

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn
question_text: Which river forms part of the international boundary between Ethiopia and Sudan?
option_b: Genale river
option_c: Baro and Tekeze rivers
option_d: Abay river
explanation: Baro and Tekeze rivers form parts of the western border with Sudan.

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn

option_b: The Baro plains

explanation: The Rift Valley region features closed inland drainage basins with no outlet to the sea.

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn

option_b: Kolla (Hot Zone)

option_c: Tropical monsoon climate modified by altitude
option_d: Equatorial rainforest climate
explanation: Ethiopia experiences a tropical monsoon climate heavily modified by rugged relief and elevation.

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn

option_c: North-Westerly winds
option_d: South-Westerly monsoon winds (from Atlantic/Indian ocean)
explanation: South-Westerly monsoons bring the main Kiremt rainy season (June to September).

subject: Geography_of_Ethiopia_and_the_Horn

option_d: Tseday
explanation: Belg is the spring minor rainy season important for southern and eastern agricultural areas.
